I picked up this game during the last big Steam sale and it's been sitting in my 'backlog' list ever since. I kicked it off today and it has turned out to be one of the funniest games I've experienced in a long time. I started playing it like any other game (finding the straight path through to success) and finished all episodes in about 30 minutes. Even on sale, this seemed a bit short for the price. Then I realized there were 80 steam achievements so I had obviously missed something.

On my second time through, I became completely engrossed and spent 3 1/2 hours combing the first 3 sections for character bios, achievement items, and failure points. The writing is creative and very witty, with regular pop culture references that are fun to recognize. Plus, the animation with stick figures, a well crafted sound track, and the ridiculous outcomes of my choices have kept me laughing most of the time. It is a classic game, brilliant in its own way, and just plain fun to play. 

There are no puzzles and no dialog trees. No walking around or collecting inventory. Just clicking on decision points (should I attack with a knife or a yo-yo? should I dig into the bank or blow through the wall?) and delightful animation. Even the combat is humorous. The hardest part of the game is that, on occasion, quick reflexes are required to click on a fleeting image for some of the achievements. Other than that, just sit back and exercise every available option for the pure fun of watching what happens. If you are looking for an entertaining way to spend COVID quarantine time, then I highly recommend hanging out with Henry Stickmin!

In the fall of 2010, I went on a now defunct website called Stickpage.com.  I played a flash game on there called "escaping the prison."  I enjoyed it, even if I wasn't invested in gaming and internet culture enough to get most of the jokes.
Around a year later, they made a new game, entitled Stealing the Diamond.  I played this, and similarly I enjoyed this game too.  I always thought it was cool how everything except the character designs--they're stick figures.--was well drawn and fun to look at.
When they made yet another game, Infiltrating the Airship, I played it almost immediately after release.  I played it TO DEATH.  It never got old to me.  Similarly, two years later, they made yet ANOTHER game; Fleeing the complex.  It was by this point that the games had gotten popular due to Youtubers such as Markiplier and Jacksepticeye playing them.
The reason I bring all this up is to show how much of a fan service this game and this series is.  The creators new that flash games were going to be extinct, so they made a bundle of their games, and even modified them.  This is a game full of humor, likable characters, and even some sad moments [you've seen the memes, you know what I'm talking about].  They put way more effort into this than they had to, and for that, this game deserves all the praise in the world.

10/10.

Unlike most people, I played the Henry Stickmin Collection with no prior experience with any of the flash games that make up this series. I have never once played one of these games, and my only real exposure to it was watching a YouTuber I like play "Stealing the Diamond" about three years ago. So, I don't have any nostalgia tinted goggles influencing me here.

So, what do I think? The Henry Stickmin Collection is incredible. These games are so much fun, they're wacky, and they make choice based elements and quick time events, two gameplay elements that are usually shoehorned into games as cheap gimmicks, actually fun. And that's all the gameplay that there is!

There are 6 main stories that you go through here. They start off shorter, and get progressively more involved with each entry. If I had to choose one as my favorite, it would definitely be Completing the Mission, which is the last game in the Collection, made exclusively for it, and by far the largest and most passionately created.

There are a ton of achievements, 82 in all, which aren't super challenging to do, but take time, and are random and fun. Bios, information about the random characters, are collectibles that you receive for right-clicking on each character that you come into contact with. I personally enjoyed this aspect of the game, as I like collectibles, and found the bio descriptions hilarious and full of humorous references (which describes the game as a whole.

The only bad thing I have to say about this game would be the bugs. First of all, the game, by default, plays in small window. You can turn on fullscreen, but when you do, you get a warning message that this makes the game unstable, and prone to freezing and crashing. I can confirm that this is definitely the case, as I had my game crash about once every 20 minutes. It's not that big a deal, as you can just restart it, and you don't lose progress, but it's very annoying. That's the most important thing that the developers absolutely NEED to fix!

Second, there are times in the animation where the frame rate just plummets for a couple of seconds for no reason. It's not always in the same spot either, because if you come back later and replay that scene, it will work fine. It appears to just be poor optimization, and should also be addressed.

Other than that, I can't say anything bad about this game. I absolutely loved it, and I think fans of this series, or people who like quirky indie games in general, will get a lot of enjoyment out of this!

I personally don't think $15 is too high a price for this game, as it really is a quality game. Some people seem to think that if you don't get a certain number of hours of entertainment out of a game, that it isn't worth the money. I don't necessarily agree, because I think shorter titles that maintain a high and consistent quality experience for 10 hours are far more worth the money than one where half of the gameplay is busy work for 40 hours. Regardless, if you don't think 10 hours of gameplay is enough to warrant a $15 purchase, then I'd recommend you wait for a sale. I can easily see this going for $5 during a holiday sale.

I hope you found this review helpful! Please leave me a rating, and give me your thoughts in the comments, as I would love to hear feedback, ideas, and what personal experiences you've had with this title.

Ok so first you need to know a little background. These games were my childhood and I always have a place in my heart for this franchise. When I heard the final game was coming 1 or 2 years ago I waited in anticipation and now The Henry Stickmin Collection is finally hear, but is it wor-

Yes. 

Let's start with the first game in the collection, Breaking The Bank Remastered:
There's not much to say about this game as it's incredibly short but sets up the series. The fails and jokes can give you a quick smirk or laugh but that's pretty much it. Still, pretty fun if you want a quick laugh. 


Escaping The Prison Remastered:

This was the first one I played back when it was a small game you'd find on NotDoppler. I loved this game growing up and still do. The slapstick comedy is hilarious and it's a fun game that brought back a lot of memories of me inside on a snow day laughing my organs out when you try to use the grenade belt. Overall, pretty fun to play especially if you're with friends,


Stealing The Diamond Remastred:

To some it up, this is the funniest one in the entire collection (until I played Completing The Mission). Nearly every fail or reference had me laughing badly and the alternative paths you can make in this game are much better than the ones in Escaping The Prison. Even though there were a LOT of references in this one it never ceased to stop my enjoyment, overall I'd say this is my favourite when it comes to the remastered games, but second favourite when putting in Completing The Mission.


Infiltrating The Airship Remastered: 

Ah, I remember being in a library playing this game and being bummed out when my 1 hour screentime limit stopped me from playing the rest of the game. I was so bummed out I immediately went on the next computer, then I got told I wasn't allowed to do tha- oh, anyway. This games pretty good, it introduced Charles and the Toppat Clan, the slapstick comedy is as always, funny as hell. This one's pretty good but I don't have much to say about it.


Fleeing The Complex Remastered: 

You have no idea how excited I was in 2015 or 2016 when I saw via Markiplier that this game had released. This one's packed to the brim with references, alternative routes and of course, fails. The fails in this game were some of the best before Completing The Mission, as always another fun game from Puffball.


Completing The Mission:

No arguing about it, this games the best in the entire series. There are 16 endings and each feels perfect for their respected path. This is the funniest game in the entire series and was a wild ride of laughs, shocks and surprises. A whole bag of references are in this game and they are all perfect. Each path feels fun and entertaining as each is almost completely different from the rest. This is the perfect send off for Henry Stickmen.


This collection has a lot of fun achievements and a new feature, bios. Every single character in this collection has a name and bio which helps make this stickman universe feel even bigger. Breaking The Bank-Escaping The Complex is also completely reanimated (remastered) and it helps put that extra bit of life into this franchise.

So overall, this game is worth the price for sure. This collection (in my opinion) is perfect in every way.

Finally, I would like to say thank you to Puffballs United, this franchise was my childhood and I can't thank them enough for all the great memories they've given me. From the bottom of my heart, thank you so much Puffballs United, you outdid yourself with this and I couldn't have been happier.

God this feels like my childhood finally wrapped up over all these years. I remember getting into these games all the way back when i was fairly new in elementary school, and now here i am a mere week from going into college. I can only imagine what will be coming next, both with PuffballsUnited and everything else in the future.

This game, I absolutely recommend it to anyone who wants a great laugh and a mass cumulation of memes and puns across almost a whole decade

This is quite possibly "'THE" single greatest game to have ever graced God's green Earth. [strike] Might be banging it on a bit here [/strike]

You play as the titular character know as Henry Stickmin as you try to get yourself out of (or usually into) sticky (pun intended) situations, through a choose your own adventure format. These choices can progress you through a branching  path of endings or result in one of numerous humorous fails.

The collection itself contains six games five of which are remasters of the previous flash games and the sixth being a brand new entry to the series 'completing the mission' (CTM). CTM will require you to go through the whole series of games to access and will involve mixing and matching the endings of Infiltrating the Airship, and Fleeing the Complex in order to play, and create several different stories based on the different endings.

Pros:
[list]
    [*]Funny and light-hearted
    [*]Won't explode your computer (it's literally point and click stickmen)
    [*]Good few hours of laughs if you like stupid humour and references. This game does not take itself seriously 
    [*]A decent amount of secrets, collectables and achievements to get (seriously they made a 1-2 sentence bio for every stickfigure that appears in the game, again full of stupid jokes and references
    [*]The game itself is very responsive and the menus are really nice and easy to navigate and you can be zooming all over the game in no time.
    [*] The animations and music are great
[/list]

Cons:
[list]
    [*]I know I personally didn't have a huge issue with the price cause i had a blast, some might due to the overall time and simplicity of the game.
    [*]The collection itself doesn't have a lot of replay ability besides looking for achievements or wanting to re-watch your favourite endings/fails, but does contain an option to reset game data to start over again
    [*]Probably my biggest issue with this game is it's lack of options, I mean i don't expect this game to have graphic settings or fps counter (though that would be hilarious) I would have hoped for an option to adjust the volume. This is probably really nit-picky but was a little annoying that i basically couldn't do anything sound related when playing the game.
    [*]The collectables can be really tedious especially the bios in CTM where there is just so many but again that's only if you wanna 100% ace the game (which I did just for laughs, thought it would pretty funny to title myself Ace stickmin)

Overall Henry stickmin collection is a quick and fun time waster, with some good old stupid humour, that you can't go wrong with. I absolutely recommend this game 

Final note: anything involving Charles is amazing and he has the greatest plans

The humor is extremely subtle, and without a solid grasp of cartoon physics most of the jokes will fly directly through a typical viewer's head. the virgin among us vs THE CHAD HENRY STICKMIN 

In all seriousness, I, like many others, played these games during my childhood, and it's been such a pleasure to see this series evolve alongside the internet over the years. The 5 original Henry Stickmin games that you all know and love are included in this collection. They are: 

Breaking the Bank 
Escaping the Prison
Stealing the Diamond
Infiltrating the Airship (my personal favourite)
Fleeing the Complex

All of these games have been updated with improved animations and artwork, along with some other tweaks and QOL improvements here and there. Sadly, some of the jokes and pop-culture references had to be changed to avoid copyright issues. Thankfully, a lot of the gags remain intact, and the ones that were changed are either extremely similar to how they were in the original flash versions, or are just as humorous. 

The final instalment, Completing the Mission, exclusive to this collection, is crammed with as many references, callbacks  and fan-service moments as you can imagine, and even manages to answer one of the biggest questions fans have had since the series began. It's also the largest game in the collection by far. Overall, with 16[spoiler]?[/spoiler] equally canon endings, this is a solid, satisfying and action-packed conclusion to this classic piece of internet history. 

I do have a few nitpicks with this collection. A handful of references to internet memes and pop-culture in the older games have, in my opinion, not aged too well, so they can be slightly painful to sit through. Completing the Mission also makes this same mistake at some points, and I feel like some of the jokes/references in that game in particular will be even more dated and painful to look back on in a few years [strike] especially when you consider how much worse modern internet humour is. [/strike] 

The collection is also prone to crashing occasionally. It most often happens in full screen mode. There is a way to enter full screen without selecting it in the settings (it involves editing the game files so I won't bother explaining it here), but that doesn't seem to prevent crashes. 

Lastly, this whole collection is pretty short, even if going for 100% completion. The games are a great time so I'd say I got my money's worth, but for those who are on the fence, get it on sale. 

TL;DR - If you enjoyed these games while growing up, get this collection. You're sure to have a nostalgia overload, and you'll be smiling by the end. 

It's been a wild ride, but 12 years and 6 games later, PuffballsUnited has Completed the Mission. Long live Henry Stickmin, and long live Newgrounds.

[i]Henry Stickmin Collection[/i] is a series of point-and-click choose your own adventure-games developed by PuffballsUnited and published by Innersloth.

[b]Story[/b]
Henry Stickmin Collection is an epic saga spanning across 6 games, telling a story of titular Henry Stickmin, a stickman who starts off the series as a small crimimal hoping for quick cash, but as his ventures go on, he gets involved with large criminal organization and ends up being a part of global conspiracy.

First 5 games from said series were originally released as free to play browser based games on Stickpage and Newgrounds, with final, 6th chapter titled "Complete the Mission" developed for this particular collection/release!

[b]Gameplay[/b]
Henry Stickmin is all about pointing and clicking to decide the fate of our hero. You can safely ditch the keyboard for this one, mouse only will do!
You get a selection of choices to move forward, and you select it by, yes you guessed it, pointing and clicking on an option! These go two ways, either you fail and retry, or you make progress to next choice. Simple? Simple.
Game provides occasionally a Quick Time Event where you have to select an option in a limited amount of time, or to click at certain direction to not fail.

Outside of main clicking, game has side clicking as well. You can click on characters you encounter to add them to your acts and later on read their bios, or you can click on environment to discover (or attempt to) many secrets and references hidden across the games!

[b]Playtime and replayability[/b]
Completing everything HSC had to offer took me 5 hours, beating only games without any character/achievement hunt will probably take you an hour, perhaps two.
Replayability is key here, afterall you just have to check all the fails game provided for your enjoyment, no?

[b]Pros and cons[/b]
Henry Stickmin is a short and simple game that will make you laugh with all the hilarious fails awaiting to be discovered, and with decent story following all those storylines you can choose from. Easy controls, decent soundtrack, even visually it ain't shabby, especially final chapter (previous ones also got remastered for this release to look better!). Bios, previously mentioned fails and ton of references you can find make it for a nice game to replay.
Bear in mind games have their age so some references might be tad older and perhaps slightly forgotten by sands of time.

Only issue is drop in performance that happens when you play the game in fullscreen mode, but it's not something horrible.

[b]Final words and conclusion[/b]
Whole Collection is a nice way to keep Flash games nostalgia alive and I hope to see more flash games appear on other platforms.

Henry Stickmin games truly embodies the joys of the 2000s era passion of internet and gaming culture. There are references galore to all sorts of legends of gaming and past icons of the internet. Every time I see something I recognize, it warms my heart up. If I don't recognize something, the game's scenarios are funny enough on their own where reference context is not needed to enjoy it.

These games feel like it's part Choose your own adventure books, part TellTale games story telling, and part visual novel. It's a game about a rookie thief who has the weirdest knack of using wacky items to get himself out of the wildest situations to steal whatever he wants or fail spectacularly. With a surprisingly elaborate story and characters for a game of this caliber.

The "story/progression" of the game is all visual so there is not much interaction. You just watch the numerous cutscenes as they come. However, you can choose an item or action at the end of cutscenes to see if you can progress or get out of whatever wacky situation Henry gets to. These items or actions can either progress, give you a different story branch, or more often than not will give you a "FAIL". There is no way to guess what the correct choices are and that's where the fun of this series is at. You never know if some dumb item will actually help you or if an item should work in a situation just fail in a hilarious way.

For returning fans from the old Newgrounds game along with updated graphics, there is expanded "lore" from all the character profiles you collect by clicking on the NPCs during cutscenes. The more copyright infringing items are also visually changed in this collection to be more "legally distinct" which can be entertaining to see differences. And of course, the new collection exclusive game, Completing the Mission, which allows you to start with previous ending and wraps up the Henry Stickmin saga.

For newcomers, this is a great way to experience the Newgrounds/ early internet culture of the day. I do recommend playing the original flash games for free on Newgrounds since the blatant references are so much more fun to see rather than "legally distinct" item references but the same joy in recognizing a reference is still here in the collection. Get this game on a discount. There isn't that much content in games like this and your millage may vary on humor since it is pretty old. 
(You can also watch gameplay videos of this. It takes away the fun of making the first choice for yourself but the cutscenes and FAILS are the main appeal of the game anyways. Also the Let's Players who play this game may also add more to entertainment as well.)

Way back in the days of Newgrounds, stick figures roamed the landscape. There was this problem, see: A lot of people wanted to be popular Flash animators but had either limited talent or simply no talent for human figures. Thus stickman animations were born, freeing up the animator from working on complex designs or backgrounds so they could focus on the motion and expressiveness of the figure.

That's not calling them low-effort, of course. Here in the Henry Stickmin Collection we find some of the higher-effort stick-figure games. Playing out like choose-your-own-adventure interactive movies, you could draw a straight line from FMV games of the past right to here. You're in a Situation. Some options appear. Pick one. Either you succeed or you fail. Keep going 'til the game is complete.

Reader, you want to fail. You want to fail dozens of times, so you can see Henry get disintegrated, blown into space, dumped in the ocean, thrown off cliffs, punched, get looked at funny and accidentally sink to the core of the Earth. The failures are why you're here, although eventually you'll want to actually finish the games in the collection too.

🕹️ The Henry Stickmin Collection

A fun, lighthearted, and totally meme-fueled game that openly parodies everything we love about gaming.
It’s packed with references to games, movies, memes, and pop culture, and you need to be a bit of an “old-school gamer” to catch them all.

At first glance, it seems like a silly joke — just click and watch the chaos unfold — but soon you realize it’s actually a clever, creative, and lovingly made parody project.
The game feels like an interactive cartoon, full of unexpected twists, ridiculous failures, and surprisingly funny outcomes.

✅ Pros:
✔ Hilarious, self-aware humor.
✔ Tons of references, Easter eggs, and nods to classic games and movies.
✔ Many endings and ways to complete each episode.
✔ Nostalgic Flash-era style and charm.
✔ Simple but recognizable and charming art direction.
✔ Energetic soundtrack that perfectly fits the tone.

❌ Cons:
➖ Occasional crashes or freezes during cutscenes.
➖ The humor won’t land for everyone — it’s absurd, chaotic, and sometimes childish.
➖ No traditional gameplay — it’s mostly an interactive story.
➖ Can feel short if you rush through all episodes.

📝 Conclusion
The Henry Stickmin Collection reminds us why games exist in the first place — for fun.
It’s not deep or emotional, but it’s filled with creativity, nostalgia, and a kind of chaotic joy that few modern games manage to capture.

👉 Rating: 8/10. Fun, chaotic, full of charm — not a masterpiece, but absolutely delightful.

🎮 Fun Facts:
• The collection includes all six Stickmin games, from Breaking the Bank to Completing the Mission.
• Created by Marcus Bromander (PuffballsUnited) — one of the developers of Among Us.
• Originally released as Flash games — this version is a full remaster.
• Features over 100 unique endings and hundreds of hilarious fail scenarios.
• Includes Easter eggs and parodies of Skyrim, Metal Gear, Minecraft, Star Wars, and many more classics.

The Henry Stickmin Collection is the classic flash game series remastered, with a whole new adventure for Henry added in at the end. The game is not about the gameplay, being just a simple point and click choose your own adventure game. It's strong suite is it's comedy and overall funny moments in the story, dialog and actions of the characters. The game is one of the most clever and successful executions of referential jokes and memes in a video game, while other games might have an easter egg or something of that sort, Henry Stickmin uses them as their main focal point. 

The game is about making decisions and achieving multiple endings, but also the main point is to see how much you can fail. There is no fail state, this game is all about just enjoying everything that happens and having a fun time discovering everything.

The comedy is charming as it is still funny, holding up even after so many years of the originals releasing. The only downsides are that the game doesn't hold much replay value after completing it and that the game sometimes crashes or lags with the animation.

Overall the game is supposed to be an experience and that for sure it is, I honestly recommend The Henry Stickmin Collection to anyone, its just that easily accessible.

For fans of old Flash games, Henry Stickmin needs little introduction. The Collection is every single Henry Stickmin game, from "Breaking the Bank" to "Fleeing the Complex", with an additional story, "Completing the Mission", for those who want to see how every possible combination of endings affects the overarching story of Henry and his arch-nemeses, the haberdashery-loving Toppat Clan. In my opinion, one more campaign after the "Multiverse Imbalance" ending would've made a perfect epilogue... but I understand the time and painstaking effort these games take to make, so I'm satisfied with what I got. Still, this collection gets a solid B+ from me.

The gameplay is really simple. It's a Flash animation. Every so often, you'll get the opportunity to pick one of a few options for Henry to choose, and then watch the animation that unfolds. You'll either progress the story or (much more often) fail in spectacular fashion — there are actually achievements for failing in every possible way. The gameplay is trial and error, but in the best way: your many, many "failures" feel more like successes, because you'll be stifling the urge to laugh.

That's not to say Henry Stickmin is a flawless game series. A few points of critique: the secret achievements can be a little obscure, and collecting all of the biographies will eventually require you to right-click on characters who appear for literal fractions of a second. If you don't pull up the wiki, you're in for some really frustrating backtracking. Also, once you've played through all the games, there isn't too much replay value unless you're dying to see everything over again.

I recommend Henry Stickmin to anyone who wants to relive the early 2000s golden age of Flash games and silly video game references, to animation fans, and to people who like some good old-fashioned slapstick.
